assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.

fresh_terms.name: ~id
fresh_terms.purpose: random message identifier selected by C; used in the AS key request, inside the authenticator encrypted for S, and in the client's id+1 response check

fresh_terms.name: ~tsC
fresh_terms.purpose: timestamp/current-time token included by C in the authenticator; exact clock semantics are not specified

fresh_terms.name: ~sidS
fresh_terms.purpose: request identifier used if S obtains C's public key from AS by the same protocol; inferred from the described optional public-key lookup

long_term_keys.name: ltkC
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for ltkC; public key pk(ltkC) may be obtained from AS or cache; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if modeled

long_term_keys.name: ltkS
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for ltkS; public key pk(ltkS) is stored by AS and sent to C; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if modeled

long_term_keys.name: ltkAS
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for ltkAS; pk(ltkAS) is assumed trusted by parties that verify/recover AS replies; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if modeled

messages.label: M2a_C_AS_ServerKeyRequest
messages.meaning: C asks AS for the public key of server S, carrying the randomly selected message identifier id in cleartext.

messages.label: M2b_AS_C_ServerKeyReply
messages.meaning: AS returns S's public key PKs to C. The protected block contains AS, C, id, and PKs; it does not contain the server identity S.
messages.protection: private-key-encryption/signature-style integrity by AS with public recovery using pk(ltkAS); no confidentiality

messages.label: M2c_C_S_Authenticator
messages.term: <C, S, privenc(<C, ~tsC, lifeC, aenc(~id, pk(ltkS))>, ltkC)>
messages.meaning: C sends the authenticator to S. The outer protected block states C, timestamp, lifetime, and an inner encryption of id under S's public key. The outer protected block does not include S.
messages.protection: outer private-key-encryption/signature-style integrity by C with public recovery using pk(ltkC); inner public-key encryption of id to S
receiver_must_treat_as_opaque: outer privenc block until S has pk(ltkC) from cache or AS lookup
inner aenc(~id, pk(ltkS)) is opaque to parties without ltkS

messages.label: M2d_S_AS_ClientKeyRequest
messages.meaning: If S does not already have C's public key PKc, S obtains it from AS using the same public-key lookup protocol as the client.

messages.label: M2e_AS_S_ClientKeyReply
messages.meaning: AS returns C's public key PKc to S using the same reply format as M2b, with S as the requester and C as the requested principal.
messages.protection: private-key-encryption/signature-style integrity by AS with public recovery using pk(ltkAS); no confidentiality

messages.label: M2f_S_C_ReturnIdPlusOne
messages.meaning: After accepting the authenticator, S decrypts the inner id using ltkS, computes id+1, and returns S and id+1 encrypted under C's public key. In the honest flow id_dec equals ~id.
messages.protection: public-key encryption to C; no server signature; intended server authentication relies on S learning id_dec from the authenticator
receiver_must_treat_as_opaque: ciphertext aenc(<S, plus1(id_dec)>, pk(ltkC)) is opaque to parties without ltkC

checks.condition: Look up pk(ltkS) in AS database for the server name S received in M2a.
Recover pubdec(privenc(<AS,C,~id,PKs>,ltkAS), pk(ltkAS)) and check AS, C, and ~id match the outstanding request.
Associate the returned PKs with the requested server S from local request state; note that S is not inside the protected M2b block.
If S lacks C's public key PKc, start the same AS public-key lookup protocol; otherwise use cached PKc.
Look up pk(ltkC) in AS database for the client name C requested by S.
If M2e is used, recover pubdec(privenc(<AS,S,~sidS,PKc>,ltkAS), pk(ltkAS)) and check AS, S, and ~sidS match the outstanding lookup request.
Recover the authenticator outer block using pk(ltkC): pubdec(privenc(<C_inner,ts_dec,life_dec,cid>,ltkC), pk(ltkC)) = <C_inner,ts_dec,life_dec,cid>.
Compare C_inner recovered from the protected authenticator with the cleartext sender name C at the top of M2c; accept only if equal.
Use timestamp ts_dec and lifetime life_dec to detect replay attacks, represented abstractly as valid_lifetime(ts_dec, life_dec) if the modeling contract includes time.
Decrypt cid = aenc(id_dec, pk(ltkS)) using ltkS to recover id_dec before computing plus1(id_dec).
Decrypt aenc(<S_reply,idplus>, pk(ltkC)) using ltkC to recover S_reply and idplus.
Check idplus equals plus1(~id). The source explicitly states this value check; explicit comparison of S_reply to expected S is not stated.

events.name: Secret
events.when: C generates the random message identifier ~id before sending M2a

events.name: AS_IssuesServerKey
events.when: AS replies to C with M2b after database lookup

events.name: C_AcceptsServerKey
events.when: C recovers and accepts M2b for its outstanding request

events.name: Running_A
events.when: C sends the authenticator M2c intended for S

events.name: S_RequestsClientKey
events.when: S lacks PKc and sends M2d

events.name: AS_IssuesClientKey
events.when: AS replies to S with M2e after database lookup

events.name: Commit_B
events.when: S accepts the authenticator after recovering the outer block, comparing client names, optionally checking timestamp/life, and decrypting id_dec

events.name: Running_B
events.when: S sends M2f containing plus1(id_dec) encrypted to C

events.name: S_AcceptsClient
events.when: S concludes that the message sender is C

events.name: Commit_A
events.when: C decrypts M2f and checks that the returned value is plus1(~id)

events.name: C_AcceptsServer
events.when: C trusts that the response was returned by the server after the id+1 check

claims.intent: There exists an honest execution in which C obtains S's public key from AS, sends the authenticator, S obtains or uses C's public key, S returns id+1, and C completes.
claims.witness: Honest trace M2a, M2b, M2c, optional M2d/M2e if PKc not cached, then M2f with id_dec = ~id.

claims.intent: Secrecy of the client-selected random identifier ~id/session value associated with C and S; exact benchmark secret term was not described, so this IR maps it to id.
claims.witness: Unknown supplied counterexample; attack surface preserved because ~id appears in clear in M2a and AS/private-key-encrypted fields are public-recoverable.

claims.intent: Injective agreement for role B interpreted as server S: each Commit_B(S,C,id) should correspond to a unique earlier Running_A(C,S,id).
claims.witness: Unknown supplied counterexample; preserve absence of S inside the protected authenticator and AS reply fields.

claims.intent: Non-injective agreement for role B interpreted as server S: each Commit_B(S,C,id) should correspond to an earlier Running_A(C,S,id).
claims.witness: Unknown supplied counterexample; preserve server-side checks exactly as described.

claims.intent: Injective agreement for role A interpreted as client C: each Commit_A(C,S,id) should correspond to a unique earlier Running_B(S,C,id).
claims.witness: Unknown supplied counterexample; preserve that M2f is only public-key encrypted to C and is not signed by S.

claims.intent: Non-injective agreement for role A interpreted as client C: each Commit_A(C,S,id) should correspond to an earlier Running_B(S,C,id).
claims.witness: Unknown supplied counterexample; preserve C's explicit check of id+1 without adding an unsupported server signature.

claims.intent: Automatically generated source/typing-style sanity goal for received values and protocol constructors.
event_schema: AUTO_typing source constraints over M2a-M2f terms
claims.witness: No concrete witness supplied; expected to hold for all traces according to user-supplied metadata.

compromise.policy: No compromise, reveal, or corruption behavior is described in the protocol input or user goals. Long-term private keys ltkC, ltkS, and ltkAS remain private setup/state unless explicit Reveal(...) rules are added by a later modeling contract; claims above have no stated reveal exceptions.

abstractions: PKc, PKs, and PKas are represented as pk(ltkC), pk(ltkS), and pk(ltkAS).
AS database lookup is abstracted as trusted setup facts mapping C to pk(ltkC) and S to pk(ltkS).
The optional S-to-AS client-key retrieval is modeled as M2d/M2e, inferred from 'using the same protocol as the client'; if S has cached PKc then M2d/M2e may be skipped.
Timestamp and lifetime are represented symbolically by ~tsC and lifeC; replay prevention is an abstract check valid_lifetime(ts,life) unless a later contract defines concrete time.
id+1 is represented by plus1(id) without arithmetic equations.
Recoverable private-key encryption with SK is modeled separately from confidentiality-providing public-key encryption with PK.
modeling_assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.
C and S know or can trust pk(ltkAS) sufficiently to recover and validate AS replies.
The AS database is authoritative for principal-to-public-key bindings but the exact database enrollment protocol is out of scope.
The message identifier id in M2a, M2b, M2c, and M2f is the same value in the intended honest run.

The source says M2b is encrypted to prevent modification; because the notation uses SKas and later text says public keys are used for decryption of SK-protected data, this IR models SK-protection as integrity/authenticity rather than confidentiality.
resolved_open_questions: Parsed {m}SKx as recoverable signature/private-key encryption, not as confidentiality, because the protocol explicitly describes public-key recovery/decryption and anti-modification protection.
Mapped role A in user-supplied authentication lemma names to client C and role B to server S; this mapping is recorded as an assumption because the goal metadata did not define A/B.
Modeled the server's optional retrieval of PKc using the same C-AS lookup pattern because the description explicitly says S uses the same protocol as the client.

semantic_constraints.policy: M2a sends ~id in cleartext. Any secrecy claim over ~id must account for this explicit disclosure.
M2b's protected block is <AS,C,id,PKs>; it does not cryptographically include the requested server name S.
C's association of returned PKs with S relies on local request state and AS behavior, not on an S field inside M2b.
M2c's outer protected authenticator block is <C,timestamp,life,{id}PKs>; it does not cryptographically include S, although S appears in the cleartext message header.
S's stated client-authentication check is specifically to recover C from the protected block and compare it with the cleartext sender name at the top of M2c.
The server must decrypt the inner aenc(id,pk(ltkS)) with ltkS to produce id+1, although the description lists this implicitly through the later M2f response.
M2f is encrypted to C under PKc but is not signed or private-key-encrypted by S; C's trust is based on the returned plus1(id) value.
The source explicitly states C checks that the returned value is id+1; it does not explicitly state that C compares the S field inside the decrypted M2f payload with expected S.
Timestamp/lifetime replay detection is semantically present but underspecified; do not silently replace it with nonce-based freshness or omit it without recording the abstraction.
No reveal or compromise exceptions are present for the supplied authentication or secrecy goals.
